audit.why: Mundo owns levels 2-3 and the item phase, with Skill at 1, 4-5 and 6. That matches the packet levelChart exactly and matches a 47.14 win rate — Sejuani losing, but not by the margin a fully conceded lane would imply. Level 6 being Skill rather than hers is right, for the reason given under point 4: the ultimate does not simply win the fight, it has to be sequenced behind his passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and whys[4] present level 6 as a clean kill window: throw R from outside his range, chain the stun, done.
audit.why: It is a kill window, but not in that order, and the order is the entire spike. Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilising effect that hits him — so an opening Glacial Prison is absorbed by his passive and the chain never starts. The correct sequence is Permafrost first to burn the passive, then the R. The entry as written teaches the reader to spend a 120-second ultimate on the one thing guaranteed to eat it, and then wonder why level 6 never converts.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and spikes[1].text now state the passive and give the order explicitly: Permafrost to pop the cannister, then Glacial Prison.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (E Permafrost cd 1.5; R Glacial Prison cd 120/105/90)

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is absent from every field in both layers. The entry never mentions that Mundo resists the first immobilise, never mentions the cannister, and never mentions that picking it up refunds him health and shortens the passive's cooldown. Frost Armor's slow immunity against Infected Bonesaw is also absent, and 'Permafrost passive/armor' appears in whys[3], spikes[0].text, spikes[2].text, wants.foe[0] and early.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Dr. Mundo resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, instead losing Health and dropping a chemical cannister nearby. Dr. Mundo can pick it up by walking over it, restoring Health and reducing this Ability's Cooldown.' Against a champion whose entire kit is three separate immobilising effects, that passive is the matchup. It dictates cast order (Permafrost, which is 1.5s and effectively free, before Glacial Prison, which is 120s), and it creates a second decision the entry never surfaces: the cannister on the ground is a denial target, because letting him walk over it both heals him and brings the passive back sooner. Frost Armor's slow immunity is the other omission — Infected Bonesaw slows at 975 range and is his only tool for holding her, and while Frost Armor holds it does nothing.
audit.corrected: The passive is now stated in whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid, late and breakdown.cooldowns, with the correct cast order and the cannister-denial point. Frost Armor's slow immunity and the out-of-combat condition are in whys[3] and wants.foe[0].
sources: champ-data/_kits/drmundo.json (P description; Q Infected Bonesaw slow, range 975, cd 4)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] says Heart Zapper gives you an '11-second window'.
audit.why: Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15. There is no 11-second number anywhere in Mundo's kit. The error runs the wrong way for the reader — it tells them their safe window is six seconds shorter than it is, so they will step up late and give away the only reliable trade the matchup offers.
audit.corrected: wants.you[0] and breakdown.cooldowns now give 17s at rank 1; mid repeats it.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid claims your stun lasts '1.25 seconds' and late claims 'your CC chain lasts roughly 2.5 seconds'.
audit.why: Neither number appears in Riot's text for Permafrost or Glacial Prison, and I could not verify them from any local source. Precise durations are exactly the kind of figure a reader will plan a fight around, so an invented one is worse than none. I removed both rather than substituting guesses.
audit.corrected: mid and late now make the same points — that the stun buys little against his regeneration and that no single tank out-damages Maximum Dosage — without asserting durations.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (E and R descriptions carry no durations)

edits.after: From level 3 you have the full chain, but Heart Zapper explodes on the same body contact that fills your Frost gauge — he times it to fire during your engage, so he bursts and heals while your stun buys almost nothing. Only commit immediately after Heart Zapper goes dark: it is 17 seconds at rank 1. Order matters more than timing at 6. Goes Where He Pleases resists his first immobilise and drops a cannister, so spend Permafrost to burn it, then throw Glacial Prison into a Mundo who can no longer shrug it off, and call the jungle before he pops R.
edits.before: From level 3 you have Q-W-E as a full combo, but Mundo's Heart Zapper active explodes on the same body contact that triggers your Frost stacks — he is timing his W to fire during your engage animation, so he bursts and heals while you stun for 1.25 seconds of damage he simply regenerates. Only commit the Q-W-E chain immediately after his Heart Zapper goes dark: give it one full cooldown cycle, then charge in. At level 6 your Glacial Prison finally outranges his healing — throw it from max range, chain into E stun, and call the jungle before he pops R. That is your only realistic kill window in this lane.

edits.after: Accept that the 1v1 is unwinnable once Mundo finishes his first full tank item — Maximum Dosage heals a share of his missing health on a 120-second cooldown and then regenerates for a long time after, and no single tank out-damages that. Your job is to be the engage tool in 5v5s: burn his passive with Permafrost, land Glacial Prison on two or more targets at an objective, and let your team do the damage yours cannot. Mundo splits top all game — do not follow him alone; match him in wave and trade the 1v1 for a 5v4 elsewhere.
edits.before: Accept that the 1v1 is unwinnable once Mundo finishes his first full tank item with Heartsteel stacks — his Maximum Dosage heals thousands of HP on a 120-second cooldown, and your CC chain lasts roughly 2.5 seconds, not long enough to burn through it. edits.after: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: 17s at rank 1 — his burst and sustain window; trade just after he wastes it. - Goes Where He Pleases: resists your first immobilise and drops a cannister; deny the pickup or the next one comes sooner. - Maximum Dosage: 120s flat.
edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His burst + sustain window — trade just after he wastes it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your Q dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.

notes:
This was the largest single omission in the slice. Dr. Mundo's passive resists the first immobilising effect that hits him, and Sejuani's kit is three immobilising effects. Nothing in either layer mentioned it. Everything the entry said about level 6 was built on an opening Glacial Prison that his passive absorbs for free.

The cannister is also a denial target and no entry treats it as one: walking over it heals him and shortens the passive's cooldown, so standing on it is worth doing.

INVENTED NUMBERS REMOVED: 'your stun lasts 1.25 seconds' and 'your CC chain lasts roughly 2.5 seconds'. Neither is in Riot's text for Permafrost or Glacial Prison and I could not verify either locally. I did not replace them with other figures. Also corrected: Heart Zapper described as an '11-second window' when it is 17s at rank 1.

'Permafrost passive/armor' remains in spikes[0].text, spikes[2].text and early. It is Frost Armor on Fury of the North. This phrase is champion-wide across the Sejuani file — it turned up in eight of the ten matchups in this slice — and is worth one scripted pass rather than per-matchup band-limited edits.
